families.name: What the routines make reaches home
families.why: The morning Jobs run and the reflections routine put their files in the mailbox; home reads them as soon as the mailbox rings it over a connection home holds open, and at least hourly while it does or every 15 minutes while it does not, and keeps a checked copy, which is what the phone shows.

objectives.claim: When a mailbox pass goes wrong in more than one place, each one is reported.
objectives.requirement: When independent phases of one pass fail (inbound, filing, outbound, asks, archive), the log names each failed phase and its failure, and mailbox_poll_failing sets each distinct failure class; what the pass did keep is kept. Within the inbound phase, the folders after a failing one wait for the next pass.
objectives.conclusion: The log now names every phase that failed, not only the first. The dashboard's failing panel shows each kind of failure, not which phase it came from, and the test shows two phases failing together.

evidence.says: A pass with both its read and its hand-over failing reports both phases, in order, and counts their one class once.
mailbox_poll_failing is labelled by failure class, not by phase, so the panel cannot say which phase failed; the log line does.
Before server#527, the phases were joined with Result::and, so only the first failure reached the log and the metric.

objectives.claim: A poller that has stopped reads as stopped, not as quiet.
objectives.requirement: The poller stamps the start of every pass, so a dashboard can tell 'nothing new' (a recent stamp) from 'not running' (an old one), and 'switched off' from both.
objectives.conclusion: The dashboard reads a stale pass stamp as red while home's server is up; if the server itself is down it shows no data rather than red, and no test holds either.

evidence.says: mailbox_poll_last_attempt_timestamp_seconds moves when a pass starts; mailbox_poll_enabled says whether it should; the SINCE LAST READ panel turns red past two intervals.
The metric contract check only shows the dashboard reads a metric the server emits, not when it moves or what the panel does with it.

objectives.claim: If the poller stops while home's server runs, you are told within 20 minutes.
objectives.requirement: While file_host answers Prometheus, an alert fires when the pass loop has not said it is alive within its heartbeat plus the pass budget plus 60 seconds (60 + 120 + 60 = 240 s), when no pass has started within the backstop interval plus the pass budget plus 60 seconds (900 + 120 + 60 = 1,080 s while home does not hold the mailbox's bell; 3,600 + 120 + 60 while it does, when every put rings home and an hour without a pass is normal), and when the metric itself is missing; it reaches the owner within 20 minutes of the poller stopping, Prometheus's 15 s evaluation and Grafana's 1 min check included, and its delivery is tested. A file_host that stops answering is FileHostDown's to report.
objectives.conclusion: While home's server runs, Slack tells you within about 5 minutes if the poller's loop stops or a pass hangs, and within about 19 minutes if it stops passing while the bell is down, inside the 20 promised; a server that stops answering is its own alert, and Grafana itself is not yet watched.

evidence.says: MailboxPollerStale fires when the loop's heartbeat (mailbox_poll_alive_timestamp_seconds, stamped every minute while idle and after each pass, never during one) is 240 s old, or when no pass has started for the current interval plus the budget plus 60 s (mailbox_poll_interval_seconds: 900 s while the bell is not held, 3,600 s while it is; paulgsc/server#500); MailboxPollerMetricsMissing when the poller is on with its stamp gone; MailboxBellDown when home has held no bell for 30 minutes. promtool tests each in CI.

Worst case while file_host answers: a dead loop or a hung pass fires at 240 s; a live loop that never passes fires at 1,080 s while the bell is down, as before the bell. Prometheus evaluates within 15 s and Grafana's rule runs within 60 s: about 315 s and 1,155 s in all. With the bell held, a loop that is alive but never passes is the timer alone failing while rings still run passes, and is told at 3,780 s; the heartbeat proves the loop alive meanwhile. The promtool tests evaluate once a minute, so they do not prove the seconds.
Grafana reads what Prometheus has firing from ALERTS and sends each alert to the Slack contact point, one message per alert.

On home on 2026-10-30, the contact point's test, a Grafana-evaluated error alert and a live FileHostDown from Prometheus (03:46 UTC, through home-alerts.yml's home_watchers route) all reached the owner's Slack.
Nothing watches Grafana itself, the one thing that delivers home's alerts.

amendments.change: The claim covers a poller that stops while home's server runs, and the bound is 20 minutes (1200 s), up from 18 (1080 s), now including delivery; the alert still fires at 1080 s, and a server that stops answering is FileHostDown's to report.
amendments.why: A message lands up to about 75 s after the rule fires (Prometheus every 15 s, Grafana every minute), so 18 minutes could hold only by cutting the interval, the 120 s pass budget or the 60 s slack; a dead server leaves the rule no data, and FileHostDown reports it within about 3.5 minutes. The owner chose the wider bound and the narrower scope over faster rules: stronger reliability waits on a real need.

amendments.change: The poller is also watched by its heartbeat (240 s), and the no-pass check follows the backstop: 1,080 s while the bell is down, 3,780 s while it is held.
amendments.why: paulgsc/server#500 (MBP2): the backstop is hourly while the mailbox's bell is held (owner, 2026-11-10) and 15 minutes while it is not (C64), so the claim's 20 minutes holds in both modes.

objectives.claim: A file put in the mailbox is at home within 20 minutes while home is up, or it shows as late.
objectives.requirement: From the Worker's commit to home's verified copy takes at most 20 minutes while home is available and the backlog is within one pass; past that, the oldest file still waiting is visible with its age, and time home was down is shown apart.
objectives.conclusion: Nothing measures how long a file waits, so whether this holds is unknown.

evidence.says: No metric records the age of the oldest file the mailbox holds that home has not kept.

While home holds the mailbox's bell, a put rings home and a pass keeps the file within seconds; while it does not, the backstop passes every 15 minutes (mailbox::UNHELD, C64), so a file waits at most 15 minutes plus a pass. Nothing yet measures the wait.

objectives.claim: A whole mailbox pass has a time limit and a request limit.
objectives.requirement: One pass ends within 120 seconds and a shared request budget, with each phase keeping a reserve; what it could not do is deferred to the next pass and recorded.
objectives.conclusion: Each request has a 30-second limit but the pass has none: at today's constants a full pass may make up to 844 calls, about 7.0 hours of waiting in the worst case.

evidence.says: Inbound 5 folders × (10 pages + 20 gets) = 150, outbound 20, the routines' indexes 4 puts (jobs, reflections, call and rust), restore 10 folders × (1 + 50) = 510, archive 12 folders × 10 pages + 20 × (get + archive) = 160: 844 calls, × 30 s ≈ 25,320 s. Filing transcripts and LeetType logs makes no call, archiving walks 12 of the 13 folders (not index), reflection's and prompt's only once one is due, and restore walks the 10 the routine can ask back (not index, reflection or prompt; paulgsc/some-ui#2178, #2179). Drama prompts share outbound's 20, and the build-journal session's lists of Drive's takes ride brief, sharing inbound's listing and its 20 gets (paulgsc/some-ui#2401).

objectives.claim: When there is nothing to do, the poller's own work stays small and counted.
objectives.requirement: With no files and no asks, a day of passes makes at most 480 mailbox requests without archiving and 2,400 with it; a change that raises either needs an amendment.
objectives.conclusion: The idle floor is known by arithmetic, not counted: no test runs a quiet day and counts the requests.

evidence.says: Hourly while home holds the mailbox's bell, every 15 minutes while it doesn't (mailbox::INTERVAL and mailbox::UNHELD; the owner's decision of 2026-11-10 and C64, paulgsc/server#500), and no two timer or catch-up passes closer than 15 minutes, so a reconnect's catch-up pass waits for that. A pass is 5 folder listings (brief, scene, drama, run, leetype); with archiving, + 10 wanted listings + 10 archive listings = 25. A bell down all day is 96 passes, 480 requests (2,400 with archiving), exactly as before the bell. A bell held all day is 24 passes, 120 (600), plus the upgrade request per reconnect. A day is never more than the 96 passes of a bell that is down: a reconnect's catch-up pass comes no sooner than 15 minutes after the last pass (C64), and only a ring or a file filed, which are work, not idle, runs a pass sooner. The bell's ping is auto-responded and costs no request. Filing LeetType logs reads home's database only. Home's index (index) adds no listing: archiving walks every folder but it (ARCHIVES), the routine's backfill rides brief, which a pass lists anyway, and with no files home computes no index. Once it holds some, it puts one only when a file it counts arrives or an open pick lapses (the index's validThrough), never for the day turning alone, so a day with no arrival and no lapse is exactly 2,400; the day a pick lapses adds one put, which is work, not idle (paulgsc/server#509). Written reflections (reflection) add no request either: home puts each when the phone sends it, which is work, never lists its asks (the routine cannot ask one back, apps/mailbox ASKED), and lists its live files only once a reflection it filed has been in the mailbox for MAILBOX_ARCHIVE_DAYS and is not yet archived, which it reads from its own tables (mailbox_repo::filed_due), so a pass with nothing to do is still 25 requests (paulgsc/some-ui#2178). Drama prompts (prompt) are the same, by the same tables (mailbox_repo::filed_due, unanswered_archives) (paulgsc/some-ui#2179). The reflections routine's index (index-reflections-*) adds no listing either: home computes it from its own tables (mailbox_repo::reflections_inputs) after each pass, and puts one only when something it counts arrives or leaves (a scene, drama, written reflection, drama prompt, list of opened lessons, reflection or scene voice note or its transcript) or a moment it carries passes (its validUntil: a group of reflections settling two hours after its newest, a reflection's or prompt's two-day wait for a voice note ending, a batch of lessons leaving the unopened window). Each such moment is owed to a record that arrived, so it adds one put on that pass, which is work, not idle, and a pass with nothing new and no moment passed is still 25 requests (an_idle_pass_makes_twenty_five_requests_and_none_reaches_the_index; paulgsc/server#509). The build-journal session's lists of the takes Drive holds add no listing either: they live in brief (drive-takes-<stamp>.json), which a pass lists anyway, and home gets one only when a new one is listed, which is work, not idle; archiving already walks brief (paulgsc/some-ui#2401). The Rust Rounds index (index-rust-*) adds no listing: home builds it from its own tables for the newest 4 weeks it holds, makes a week final once past its due, and puts only when a final week's record changes, so an idle pass is still 25 requests.

amendments.change: The idle bound is 480 mailbox requests a day without archiving and 2,400 with it, up from 384 and 1,920.
amendments.why: paulgsc/server#583 (some-ui#2026, #2027) has home read the leetype folder, so an idle pass lists five folders, and adds leetype and leetype-log to the ten folders archiving walks for asks and old files: 5 + 10 + 10 = 25 listings a pass, 96 passes a day. The owner chose the higher bound: "yes, raise the bound to 2,400".

amendments.change: The backstop is hourly while the mailbox's bell is held and 15 minutes while it is not, never closer; the idle bound stays 2,400, a bell-down day's figure.
amendments.why: paulgsc/server#500 (MBP2); the owner chose the hourly backstop, and C64 keeps 15 minutes while the bell is down so MI3 and MI4 hold.

objectives.requirement: Each Worker operation totals D1's rows read and rows written from the statements it ran, and those totals are observable without any file's name or bytes.
objectives.conclusion: D1 returns its row counts with every statement, and the Worker throws them away.

objectives.requirement: The mailbox keeps a file's bytes only until home holds it and it has been live 30 days; home keeps a row per file put, per file handed over and per Jobs event, for good; the bytes this adds per file and per day are stated from measurement.
objectives.conclusion: Each file the routines put is kept on home for good and leaves the mailbox once home holds it; how many bytes a day that adds has not been measured yet.

families.why: Home archives what has sat in the mailbox for a while; a routine that needs an old file asks for it, and home puts it back.

D1 bills rows read, not VM steps, and the index adds a write and storage per ask; neither is measured on D1.

families.name: A request the app makes stops when you stop it
families.why: The shared fetch client carries the app's reads of lessons, word lists and the NFL data; a request it keeps making after you have moved on is work for nothing.

objectives.claim: A request stops when its caller cancels it, and 'no retries' means one try.
objectives.requirement: A call makes at most 1 + its own retry count attempts; once the caller's signal aborts, no attempt starts, a waiting backoff ends, and the call rejects as cancelled, never as timed out.
objectives.conclusion: Each way a cancel can arrive is tested, and zero retries makes one attempt. The app's query hooks do not pass React's cancel along yet (some-ui#2207).

evidence.says: Before #2202, an already-cancelled call still went out, a cancel mid-flight reached nothing, and retry count 0 made 2 attempts.

families.name: A line you ask to hear is fetched once
families.why: On the home-network web build, a line's audio comes from the hosted voice service over the network; a replay tapped again before the answer arrives must not send the line again.

objectives.claim: For one line and voice, at most one request for its audio is on its way at a time.
objectives.requirement: At most 1 request in flight per line and voice (provider, voice, the whole text, format and quality). A request for a line already on its way joins it; a requester that cancels leaves only its own wait, and the request ends on its response, its timeout or the adapter's dispose. Requests in flight are bounded by the distinct lines asked for within one timeout (30 s by default).
objectives.conclusion: Tapping a replay again while the line is on its way joins the request already sent, and once it is answered the line is cached. This covers the hosted voice only: the phone's engine and the browser's own voice send nothing over the network.

evidence.says: Before the fix, K taps while a line was on its way sent K requests, K-1 of them cancelled, and nothing played until the taps paused for longer than one round trip.
Whether openai-edge-tts stops synthesizing when the connection drops is not checked. A requester's cancel no longer drops it; a timeout or a dispose still does.

families.name: A read you ask for again while it is on its way is sent once
families.why: "Try again", reopening the lesson already open, and a second scene picker all repeat a read the app already has on its way.

objectives.claim: A retry or re-selection of a read already on its way joins it; at most one request per read is running.
objectives.requirement: At most 1 request in flight per read for: "Try again" on every page that reads through queryOutcome (profile, app, sessions, a session, new session, study settings, practice, the device voice) and on TOPIK handheld's dramas, which join the fetch on its way instead of cancelling it; reopening the lesson already open in the lesson CRM, which starts nothing unless its read failed; and the scene library, loaded once per page for every picker. Requests in flight are bounded by the distinct reads asked for while one is on its way: opening another lesson still starts its own read, and the one it replaces runs on, since the CRM's read takes no cancel.
objectives.conclusion: Tapping Try again, reopening the open lesson, or opening a second scene picker while the read is on its way sends nothing more. The lesson CRM's read of a lesson you have moved away from is not stopped, and a refresh the app starts itself (an invalidation after a change) still follows TanStack's own default.

evidence.says: Before the fix, each tap of Try again on a page that still showed data sent one more GET and cancelled none of them (the query functions ignore the cancel), each click on the open lesson re-read it and reset the editor, and every mounted scene picker fetched the manifest and every scene file.

families.name: Every take says how it ended, and home hears it
families.why: A take that failed on the phone while every test was green was found only by luck (MIC0, some-ui#2370). Every real take now leaves a note of how it ended, so a failure shows in what real use leaves, not only in the steps someone thought to try (CHECKS, some-ui#2369).

objectives.claim: Every take a screen on the take kit starts ends exactly once, in an ending of the kit's closed union, and is said.
objectives.requirement: Of every take started on the kit or the pattern, exactly one ending (kept, short, early, full, failed or blocked with its reason), recorded in the kit's own step; none ends twice and none is left without one, whatever the order of taps, the microphone's answers and the clock.
objectives.conclusion: Every generated trace of taps, microphone answers and ticks over the real kit ends each take once. This is the code over a simulated microphone: a real phone's microphone is checked by nothing yet (CK5, some-ui#2384).

evidence.says: The property suite runs VC2's monitor over every generated trace of the scenario family, on the real kit and the real pattern.

objectives.claim: Every take's ending leaves a note on the phone that waits until home holds it exactly as sent, and only then leaves the phone.
objectives.requirement: Each ending the kit records is handed to the app's store once, from the screen that recorded it, with its timings and nothing of what was said. A note leaves the phone only once home has answered with it as sent; one home refused, answered otherwise or never answered stays. At most 500 wait: past that a new note is not kept, and none waiting is let go for it.
objectives.conclusion: Every ending of a take on the kit or the pattern reaches the store, and the lane lets a note go only on home's answer holding it as sent. On the phone only: whether home then keeps it is TE3's.

evidence.says: Each runtime reports the ending its step recorded, so a screen cannot leave a take out.

objectives.claim: Home keeps each note it is sent once, append-only, and answers with it as kept, so a resend stores nothing new.
objectives.requirement: A PUT of a note home lacks stores it and answers with it; the same note again is unchanged; a different note under its id is refused and nothing is replaced. A note holds the process, the screen, the ending and how it went, timings, a peak level and the build, every text field an id from the code: home refuses any other field (the owner's C3).
objectives.conclusion: Home's side is in its pull request (server: app_event_repo and handlers::app_events) and holds nothing until that merges.

evidence.says: Home serves no route for the notes until its pull request merges, so nothing it keeps can be measured yet.

objectives.claim: What the phone's app events keep (how takes ended, and whether the owner used what a pipeline offered) grows by a take or a use, and stays small.
objectives.requirement: On the phone, at most 500 events of a few hundred bytes wait, both families sharing that allowance, each leaving once home holds it, and at most 200 engagement events wait in memory for the app to set the sink. On home, one row per event, a few hundred bytes, append-only; the rate is stated from measurement.
objectives.conclusion: The phone's store is bounded at 500 events of both families; home's grows by a row per take or use, unmeasured until home's table is sampled.

evidence.says: The phone keeps at most APP_EVENTS_WAITING events, outcomes and engagement alike, and lets each go once home holds it; the engagement sink holds at most EARLY_WAITING before the app sets it.
Home's table only grows, and no sample of it has been read: it does not exist until the server's pull request merges.

families.name: Voice notes sent home get heard
families.why: The phone sends a voice note home; home transcribes it in the background, and the transcript is what the routine reads. A note I let go on the phone is set aside on home, kept, and the routines read it no more (D3).

objectives.claim: Every voice note sent home gets a transcript or a recorded reason it has none, its set-aside mark among them.
objectives.requirement: Each note home holds gets a row; a failed hearing is recorded and tried again on at most ATTEMPTS (3) passes, then stays recorded as failed, so no note is left without an outcome after three passes. A note set aside (D3) before it was heard leaves the queue, its mark the recorded reason; the phone sends that mark once for each note it set aside that home holds, and keeps it owed until home takes it. While home has no route for the mark (a server before paulgsc/server#638), the phone keeps at most ASIDE_OWED_MAX (500) owed marks; past that it drops the oldest whose notes have left the phone, and home's routines go on reading those notes.
objectives.conclusion: Every note gets a row, and a failure is retried a few times and then kept as failed. A note I let go before home heard it is not heard, and home keeps its mark saying so; the phone owes the mark at Let go, before the note is set aside, for every kind of note that can be let go, and sends it once home holds the note. While home runs a server without the mark's route, the phone keeps at most 500 marks owed, and past that the oldest of notes no longer on the phone are dropped and those notes stay read.

evidence.says: A pass gives every note a row and retries a failure a few times.
The transcriber's queue skips a note set aside, which keeps its row in voice_note_set_aside.
The voice lane sends the mark of a note set aside in each store that goes home, once home holds it, once only, and again after home found no note.

proof: some-ui:apps/www/src/lib/home-link/__tests__/voice-aside.test.ts#home's set-aside mark on a note let go on the phone (MIC2)

amendments.change: A note set aside before home heard it is no longer heard: its set-aside mark is the recorded reason it has no transcript. While home has no route for the mark, the phone keeps at most 500 owed and drops the oldest of notes no longer on it, which home then goes on reading.
amendments.why: The owner's D3 is what changes VH1: set aside means out of what routines read, kept on home, and the transcriber's queue is one of those reads. Keeping the mark in a table of its own (shape B) was the session's choice under the owner's direction to go with recommendations (some-ui#2372 comment 6559370232), as was the 500-mark cap on what the phone keeps owed for a home without the route (#2451).

families.name: Rust Rounds' programs get run on home
families.why: A Rust Rounds round sent home is kept there, and so is each week the routine puts in the mailbox (RR12, some-ui#2687); home queues each of their programs and, in the background, hands each to the sandboxed rust-runner and keeps what rustc printed, so a card can show a run made on home. A paired phone sends each round pasted on it home, and brings home's rounds and the runs recorded of them back, through its home-link lane while the app is open (RR4b, some-ui#2347); how that lane's runs went is Settings' readout of what this phone keeps on home.

objectives.claim: Every program in a round home keeps reaches an outcome that is its own: its recording, the runner's refusal of it, or that it lost the runner twice.
objectives.requirement: The recorder always runs, and each pass first reads the operator's Rust Rounds recording switch (the rust-rounds admin setting, on by default) once; while it is paused the pass asks the runner nothing, and rounds and weeks are still kept and their programs wait; a switch it cannot read skips the pass, logged at ERROR and counted on operation_errors_total{operation="rust_rounds"} as setting. While recording is on, each distinct program a stored round holds is queued once, and a pass asks about the waiting programs in arrival order under the runner's toolchain. A recording is kept as recorded, and a refusal of the program itself (malformed or too-large) as refused with its reason; either way the pass goes on. A runner that goes away after the whole request was sent, or does not answer within ASK_TIMEOUT (137 s, past its watchdog's job deadline of 132 s), is a loss held against the program (dropped or timed-out; a fault of the runner's machine after the program ran answers nothing, so it is one too), and the pass stops; at its DROPS (2)th loss, of either kind, the program is kept as runner-lost. A program kept as recorded, refused or runner-lost is never asked again under that toolchain. Anything else is an outage that keeps nothing and holds nothing against a program: a failed toolchain ask, a runner that cannot be reached or does not take the request, a refusal as wrong-toolchain, unavailable (its machine failed before the program ran) or peer, an answer that is not one, or a recording under another toolchain. The pass stops and every program waits for the next. No socket at the runner's path when the pass asks its toolchain is no runner on this machine: a deployment fact, not an outage; the pass stops as no_runner, keeps nothing, and it is logged once at WARN when first seen and once at INFO when a socket is there again, never as an error each pass; a runner that is deployed but down leaves its socket behind, so it is an outage. Every other stop but a deadline reached after at least one program was asked about is logged at ERROR and counted on operation_errors_total{operation="rust_rounds"} by its kind, as is a storage failure. So no program holds up the queue for good, and a program is blamed only for what it did.
objectives.conclusion: While recording is on, every program ends recorded, refused, or after two losses runner-lost, and an outage keeps nothing, is reported at ERROR on every pass it lasts and leaves every program for the next; while the operator has it paused, or on a machine with no runner (said once), rounds are kept and their programs wait.

evidence.says: A pass records every waiting program once, a second pass asks nothing, and a new toolchain records each program again.
A program the runner refuses as too large is kept as refused with that reason, the program behind it is recorded in the same pass, and the refused one is not asked again.

A program the runner goes away holding, and one it does not answer for in time, are each asked again and at their second loss kept as runner-lost (losses dropped, dropped, timed-out, timed-out); the program behind them is then recorded.

A runner that cannot be reached, says unavailable or answers nonsense, to the toolchain ask or a program's, keeps nothing and holds no loss against any program, three passes each; a toolchain changed mid-pass keeps nothing; each such pass is an error, and the next with the runner back records every program.
A pass that failed, or a storage failure, is logged at ERROR and added to operation_errors_total{operation="rust_rounds"} with its kind; that it is counted is read from the code, not tested.

No socket at the toolchain ask stops a pass as no_runner, three passes running, keeping nothing, holding no loss and failing none; a runner that then answers records every program, and a socket gone between the toolchain ask and a program's is an outage.
Pausing, resuming, no runner and a socket there again are each said once when they change, not every pass.
An unset switch reads as on and says it is the default, and a stored value that no longer parses is an error, not the default.
Each pass reads the switch once before it asks the runner anything, and skips while it is paused; read from the code.

amendments.change: Recording is the operator's switch, on by default, read once a pass, in place of RUST_ROUNDS_ENABLED; and no socket at the runner's path is no runner on this machine, said once at WARN and not an error each pass, where every unreachable runner was an ERROR every pass.
amendments.why: The owner made recording a lever set from the web app, with no environment limit, and asked that a missing runner be reported as a deployment fact, not an error every minute on a box that has no runner. A runner that is deployed but down still leaves its socket, so it is still an outage at ERROR every pass.

objectives.claim: A recording pass takes a bounded batch and stops at its deadline.
objectives.requirement: A pass first asks the runner its toolchain, waiting CLIENT_TIMEOUT (5 s), and only when its deadline (RUST_ROUNDS_PASS_DEADLINE_SECONDS, 600 by default) is at least MIN_DEADLINE (142 s, that wait and one program's); with less it asks nothing, which is an error. It then takes at most BATCH (20) waiting programs in arrival order, one at a time, asking about each only while its whole wait, ASK_TIMEOUT (137 s), is left before the deadline. A deadline reached after at least one program was asked about is a warning, not an error, and what a pass does not reach waits for the next. Each of a program's at most DROPS (2) losses under a toolchain costs a pass at most ASK_TIMEOUT (137 s).
objectives.conclusion: A pass records at most 20 programs, asks none it could not wait out before its deadline, and at the shortest deadline allowed still records one; the next pass takes the rest.

evidence.says: Over 21 waiting programs a pass records exactly 20 and the next the last; at exactly MIN_DEADLINE a pass records a program, 1 ms below it a pass asks nothing and fails.
A pass that runs out of time after recording a program stops with a warning, not an error.

objectives.claim: What Rust Rounds keeps on home grows by a stated model, and a round is kept until its account goes.
objectives.requirement: Home keeps each round as the phone sent it, at most 32 KiB, until its account is deleted, and each distinct program once, with one run per program and toolchain (recorded, refused or runner-lost) and at most DROPS (2) losses per program and toolchain, for good; nothing is rewritten, and its growth per round and per day is stated from measurement.
objectives.conclusion: Each round is at most 32 KiB and kept until its account goes, and each program, its one outcome under each toolchain and at most two losses are kept for good; how fast they grow is not measured yet.

evidence.says: All four tables refuse UPDATE; a round is deleted only by its account's deletion trigger, and a program, a run and a loss refuse DELETE.

Every table refuses an update and a delete while the round's account stands, and deleting an account takes its rounds and leaves the programs and their runs, which another subject's round still reads.
A round's body is refused above 32 KiB (ROUND_CEILING).
A run keeps the runner's answer, which is refused above 4 MiB (ANSWER_CEILING); the runner keeps at most 4 KiB of what a program printed on each stream.
Home samples every table's bytes once a day (storage_sample, server#551), but no round has reached home yet, so there is no growth to read.

families.name: Home follows the games of the week
families.why: Home polls ESPN's public NFL feed in the background, keeping every answer and appending each game's plays to a log, so the phone's game-day bites can later be matched to the play they are about. No route serves the log; the paired phone's game day socket (in the `websocket` module, placed in `synchronous`) reads it to offer what can be happening now, only while the socket is open.

objectives.claim: On a working store, every answer ESPN gives is kept and counted by what it was, and a fetch with no answer is counted by why.
objectives.requirement: Each response, a 429, another refusal or an unreadable body included, is kept raw before it is read, in the transaction that appends the plays read from it, and is never updated or deleted; a fetch with no answer stores nothing and is counted in game_feed_fetches_total by kind (timeout, connect, transport).
objectives.conclusion: Every answer is kept and every fetch is counted by its kind, in the store and pass tests, while the store works. A storage failure ends the pass: the answer it failed on is not kept, the fetches the pass had already made are not counted (the pass reports no counts), and FAILING shows it; what was due after it waits for the next pass.

evidence.says: Seven responses, a 429 and an HTML page among them, are all kept, read by kind, and replay to the same play log.
Kept responses and plays refuse UPDATE and DELETE.
A 429, a timeout and an HTML page are each counted by kind in one run of passes; the three answers are kept and the timeout stores nothing.

objectives.claim: A fetch that keeps failing is asked less and less often, one target at a time.
objectives.requirement: After a 429, any other refusal, an unreadable body or no answer, that target (the scoreboard, or one game's summary) waits its own cadence doubled per failure in a row, to at most GAME_FEED_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS (900), before it is asked again; its next good answer resets it.
objectives.conclusion: The pass test shows each target spacing its retries out, doubling to the cap and resetting on a good answer, but that is a spacing rule, not a budget: nothing bounds how many times a target is retried in all, so RE2 is not held.

evidence.says: 600 s doubled is capped at 900 s, the next waits 900 s more, a good answer resets the count, and a live summary waits 30 s then 60 s.

objectives.claim: Home fetches a game only while there is something to learn about it.
objectives.requirement: A wake with nothing due fetches nothing; a game's summary is fetched every live cadence (15 s) from kickoff until a summary of it says final, then never again, a restart included; a completed game first seen late is still fetched until its final summary is kept; a game still called pre or postponed is fetched only within its grace (4 h after kickoff, and 8 h once over without completing).
objectives.conclusion: The pass tests follow a game from kickoff to its final fetch and then see no fetch, see a restart skip a game it holds final, and see a late-seen completed game and a postponed one handled. Not bounded: a game the scoreboard calls completed whose own summary never reads final is fetched for as long as that lasts (every 15 s while answers parse, every 900 s while they fail), and a response's bytes are read without a limit.

evidence.says: Before kickoff only the scoreboard is fetched, a wake inside a cadence fetches nothing, and after the final summary the game is never asked again.
A restarted worker fetches only the scoreboard for a game home already holds final; a completed game first seen a day later is fetched once.
A postponed game is left after the post grace, and one still called pre past its grace waits for the scoreboard.

objectives.claim: A game feed that has stopped reads as stopped, not as a quiet week.
objectives.requirement: Every wake stamps game_feed_last_attempt_timestamp_seconds, whether or not anything is due, so a dashboard tells 'nothing to fetch' (a recent stamp) from 'not running' (an old one), and game_feed_enabled, the owner's switch as the last wake read it (1 following, 0 paused), tells 'switched off' from both; an alert tells the owner when the stamp goes stale.
objectives.conclusion: The dashboard tells a quiet week from a stopped feed, and Slack tells you within about three minutes of its last wake once it stops, or through the server-down alert if home's server stops; a feed that is on but has never woken has no alert, and Grafana itself is not yet watched.

evidence.says: The worker stamps the start of every wake before its pass; the SINCE LAST LOOK panel reads time() minus that stamp and turns red at 60 s.
GameFeedStale fires when the feed is on and its stamp is more than 120 s old; promtool tests it in CI.
Grafana reads what Prometheus has firing from ALERTS and sends each alert to the Slack contact point, one message per alert.

On home on 2026-10-30, the contact point's test, a Grafana-evaluated error alert and a live FileHostDown from Prometheus (03:46 UTC, through home-alerts.yml's home_watchers route) all reached the owner's Slack.
Nothing watches Grafana itself, the one thing that delivers home's alerts.

amendments.change: game_feed_enabled is the owner's switch on Home's switches (the game-feed setting, on by default), as each wake reads it before any fetch, in place of GAME_FEED_ENABLED read once at start.
amendments.why: The owner does not keep policy as an environment variable: whether home follows games is a switch set from the web app, as Rust Rounds recording is. The gauge still tells 'switched off' from a quiet week and from a stopped feed, so the claim holds as before.

objectives.claim: What the game feed keeps grows by a model the owner chose.
objectives.requirement: The bytes kept per followed game and per week are stated and bounded by a model the owner decided, and the play log is never traded for space.
objectives.conclusion: Since server#555, each distinct answer ESPN gives is kept once and every fetch keeps only a small row naming it, with nothing deleted and no cap on the games followed, as the owner chose; how many distinct bodies a real Sunday leaves is not measured yet.

evidence.says: game_feed_body keeps each distinct body once by its SHA-256, written with INSERT OR IGNORE and refusing UPDATE and DELETE; a response row keeps the hash and size only.

ESPN caches a summary for 5 s and a play comes about every 40 s, so most of a live game's 840 fetches (one per 15 s for 3.5 h) repeat the body before; without the dedupe the same slate was about 1.1 GB.

The ratio of response rows to bodies on a real Sunday, and their bytes from storage_sample, are not read yet: the feed was off. Home follows games by default once the game feed's switch ships, so they are measurable from the first Sunday after it deploys.

families.name: Home matches each game bite to its play
families.why: Home's reconciler, a task beside the game feed's worker, reads the feed's play log and the game's bites, and keeps for each bite the play it was about or why there was none, so every short can lay the right moment over a bite (GWB7, paulgsc/some-ui#2081). It runs whether or not home is following games, and reads only what the feed has kept; while the feed is paused no game goes final, so a pass finds only bites late for games already final.

objectives.claim: Every bite home holds with a scenario is matched to a play or marked unmatched and kept, never dropped.
objectives.requirement: Each pass over a game appends one bite_match row for each of its bites whose match changed, naming the play (same game, a play the scenario's rule accepts, at or before the bite's start on home's clock, within the broadcast-delay window, the nearest) or why there was none; bite_match refuses UPDATE and DELETE, and a reader takes each bite's newest row.
objectives.conclusion: The reconciler's test matches each bite to its play or marks it unmatched and keeps it, and the store refuses rewriting a match. Whether the match is the right play (8 in 10 on a real Sunday, #2081) is the owner's spot check, not this objective.

evidence.says: Each bite of a replayed game is matched to its play, or marked unmatched with why, and kept.

objectives.claim: A scenario proposed for a said-first bite is kept only if home's engine says it could have been happening.
objectives.requirement: A proposal (from the shot writer, GWB9) becomes an append-only bite_mapping row only if its scenario is in the catalog and replaying the engine at the bite's time offers it; a rejected one leaves the bite unmapped, never mislabelled, and the bite itself is never rewritten.
objectives.conclusion: The reconciler's test keeps a proposal the engine offered at the bite's time and refuses one it did not. Nothing calls `propose` until GWB9.

evidence.says: A proposal the engine could not have offered at the bite's time is refused and leaves the bite unmapped.

objectives.claim: A game already final is reconciled again only when it has new bites.
objectives.requirement: Every reconcile::TICK (10 minutes) the task reconciles a final game once, and again only when a bite arrived since its last pass; it runs whatever the game feed's switch says.
objectives.conclusion: The worker's test passes over a final game once, then again only after a new bite; idle, a pass reads the newest scoreboard and the games it names and writes nothing.

evidence.says: A final game is reconciled once, skipped on the next tick, and reconciled again after a new bite.

amendments.change: The reconciler always runs, a pass every reconcile::TICK, where it was spawned only while GAME_FEED_ENABLED was on and logged once and spawned nothing while it was off.
amendments.why: Whether home follows games became the owner's switch, read each wake, so it is no longer known when home starts; the reconciler runs regardless, and a pass still reconciles a final game again only when a bite arrived since its last pass. The requirement also no longer says a game in play is reconciled: the worker reconciles only final games.

objectives.claim: What the reconciler keeps grows by bites, not by passes.
objectives.requirement: A pass appends a bite_match row only for a bite whose match changed, and a bite_mapping row only for an accepted proposal, so the rows grow by about one small row per bite (more only when a later pass finds a nearer play) and never by the 10-minute tick; neither is updated or deleted but with the account.
objectives.conclusion: Both tables refuse UPDATE and leave only with the account, and the worker's test writes nothing on a tick that changes no match; at a few hundred bites a season, the rows stay in the tens of kilobytes.

evidence.says: bite_match and bite_mapping refuse UPDATE, are deleted only by their account's deletion trigger, and hold no audio or text a person said.
A tick over a game whose bites' matches did not change writes no row.
A match is added once; a later, different one is a new row.

families.name: Study nudges stay bounded
families.why: Home decides when to nudge you to study from the phone's presence and signals, and sends the nudge by push.

objectives.claim: A nudge pass ends on time, and what it did not reach waits for the next one.
objectives.requirement: A waker pass reads at most BATCH due subjects and stops at its pass deadline; a subject it never reached is left untouched and still due.
objectives.conclusion: Held by the waker's written scaling rules and their tests: a bounded batch, one deadline, nothing lost at the cut.

evidence.says: A pass that reaches its deadline leaves the subjects it never reached untouched and still due; subjects beyond a batch are finished by later passes.
The scaling rules are written down: O(1) work per signal, an indexed range read, every pass bounded by BATCH and the deadline alone.

objectives.claim: If the nudge waker stops, you are told.
objectives.requirement: An alert fires when no waker pass has started within its interval plus its pass deadline plus 60 seconds, and when its metrics are missing; its delivery is tested.
objectives.conclusion: If the waker stops, Slack tells you within about 75 s of its interval plus its deadline plus a minute, or through the server-down alert if home's server stops; Grafana itself is not yet watched.

evidence.says: NudgeWakerStale fires when no waker pass has started within its interval plus its pass deadline plus 60 s, and NudgeWakerMetricsMissing when it is on with its stamp gone; promtool tests both in CI.
Grafana reads what Prometheus has firing from ALERTS and sends each alert to the Slack contact point, one message per alert.

On home on 2026-10-30, the contact point's test, a Grafana-evaluated error alert and a live FileHostDown from Prometheus (03:46 UTC, through home-alerts.yml's home_watchers route) all reached the owner's Slack.
Nothing watches Grafana itself, the one thing that delivers home's alerts.

objectives.claim: What the study nudge keeps stays within its stated horizons.
objectives.requirement: While the nudge is on, each pass sweeps intervention_log past 90 days and activity_outcome past a year (owner, 2026-10-28), at most RETENTION_SWEEP_LIMIT = 500 rows per table per pass, so a backlog (the nudge turned on again after a long while off) is gone once the passes catch up; with it off, both keep every row. Presence leases are at most 16 per person, and the charge and gate one row per person and class, either way.
objectives.conclusion: Both sweeps run in the nudge waker, which runs only while the nudge is on, 500 rows per table per pass, so while it is on a log holds nothing past its horizon once its backlog is swept, and while it is off both logs keep every row, as stated.

evidence.says: The nudge waker, which runs prune_intervention_log and OutcomeRepository::prune, is spawned only while NUDGE_ENABLED is on: the horizons hold while it is on, and with it off both logs keep every row.
Presence leases are trimmed to the 16 newest per person on every write, on home and on the phone.

amendments.change: The horizons hold while the nudge is on; with it off, intervention_log and activity_outcome keep every row. The requirement no longer asks for the horizons whether or not the nudge is on.
amendments.why: Running both sweeps whatever the nudge's setting would delete old study rows that today's code keeps while the nudge is off. Asked under "Never lose the record", the owner chose to state the sweeps as they run rather than discard more.

families.name: The morning run leaves an outcome
families.why: The 7:52 Jobs routine runs off home, at Anthropic; a run that never starts leaves nothing behind unless something expects it.

objectives.claim: A morning run that never started shows as missing when you open Jobs, not as a quiet morning.
objectives.requirement: When the run is due and home keeps run records but holds none for today, Today says home has no record of a run, apart from a run that found nothing.
objectives.conclusion: Jobs tells a missing run apart from an empty one, once you open it.

evidence.says: Today says home has no record of a run, only from a home that keeps them.

proof: some-ui:apps/www/src/lib/jobs/__tests__/morning.test.ts#says home has no record of a run only from a home that keeps them

objectives.requirement: While file_host answers Prometheus, home expects each scheduled run by its time zone's clock, and an alert fires when none is recorded 30 minutes after it was due; it reaches the owner within 32 minutes of the due time, Prometheus's 15 s evaluation and Grafana's 1 min check included, and its delivery is tested. Grafana reads what Prometheus has firing from ALERTS and sends each alert to the Slack contact point, one message per alert.

On home on 2026-10-30, the contact point's test, a Grafana-evaluated error alert and a live FileHostDown from Prometheus (03:46 UTC, through home-alerts.yml's home_watchers route) all reached the owner's Slack.
Nothing watches Grafana itself, the one thing that delivers home's alerts.

amendments.change: The claim covers a run missed while home's server runs, and the bound is 32 minutes (1920 s) after the due time, up from 30 (1800 s), now including delivery; the alert still fires at 30 minutes, and a server that stops answering is FileHostDown's to report.
amendments.why: A message lands up to about 75 s after the rule fires (Prometheus every 15 s, Grafana every minute); a dead server leaves the rule no data, and FileHostDown reports it within about 3.5 minutes. The owner chose the wider bound and the narrower scope over faster rules: stronger reliability waits on a real need.

objectives.claim: What the Jobs notice keeps stays small.
objectives.requirement: One row per phone registered for the notice, gone when it withdraws, and one row per notice sent; the rate is stated from measurement.
objectives.conclusion: A phone's registration is one row that leaves when the phone withdraws; the record of notices sent grows by a row per notice, unmeasured.

evidence.says: jobs_notice_device is deleted on withdrawal (forget); jobs_notice_sent only grows.
Home samples every table's bytes once a day (storage_sample, server#551), but no samples have been read yet: they start once file-host is restarted on the box.

families.name: The checks themselves
families.why: Every promise above is only as good as the checks that hold it and what happens when one fails.

objectives.claim: A failing required check stops a merge, in both repositories.
objectives.requirement: main in some-ui requires CI Gate and main in the server requires its five named checks (Artifact retention, Rust lint, rust_ci, metric_contract_ci, Deny Checks Summary); a deliberately failing pull request is shown to be blocked in each, and a check fails if either repository stops requiring them. The checks a pull request passed must also have run against the main it merges into: main requires branches to be up to date before merging, or merges through a queue, and the check fails if it stops.
objectives.conclusion: A failing required check stops a merge in both repositories, as probes showed even through the owner's account. Both repositories require up-to-date branches, confirmed through their active main rules on 2026-11-08. check:branch-rules asserts the named required checks and either strict up-to-date branches or a merge queue, so disabling merge-order protection fails CI Gate and the daily check.

evidence.says: A deliberately failing pull request was refused in each repository through the owner's account: "Required status check \"CI Gate\" is failing" and "Required status check \"Artifact retention\" is failing".
The server's probe pull request, refused on a failing required check.
GET /repos/paulgsc/{some-ui,server}/rules/branches/main on 2026-10-28 required CI Gate in some-ui and the five named checks in the server.
Both repositories' active main rules require strict_required_status_checks_policy: true, confirmed on 2026-11-08 after the owner enabled the settings.
pr.yml's Repo guards job, which CI Gate needs, and the daily branch-rules.yml run the check.

amendments.change: The claim is to required checks; the server's half is its five named required checks, not one gate that waits on every check, which moved to GC5.
amendments.why: The server's checks span several workflows and a job cannot wait on another workflow's jobs, so one gate is real work (AS10), not a setting.

some-ui:packages/assurance/src/__tests__/branch-rules.test.ts#requires up-to-date branches or a merge queue

objectives.requirement: Every module in the server's route snapshot is in exactly one family or in the synchronous list, with a reason; a new module fails the check until someone places it.
objectives.conclusion: check:assurance fails a server module that is in no family and not listed as synchronous.

evidence.says: The coverage rule's test fails an unplaced and a stale module.

objectives.claim: Loosening what a promise requires shows, with who decided it.
objectives.requirement: Against the base branch, an objective is never removed, and each of these needs a new amendment linking the owner's decision: a holds that stops holding, a changed claim, requirement, kind or property, a weaker watch, a loosened or dropped bound, a retirement. A route module leaving a family for synchronous needs a decision too.

objectives.claim: The server's own checks hold its half of this ledger.
objectives.requirement: Server CI reads this ledger, fails when a server path a holds names is missing, and fails a background task that belongs to no family.
objectives.conclusion: The server's Assurance ledger job reads this ledger from main on every server pull request and fails a server proof or path that is gone and a background task in file_host that no family covers, except the 10 s gauge sweep, which only warns until the owner places it; since main requires PR gate (GC5), a red run stops a merge.

evidence.says: Its run on server#557's merged head read some-ui main: all 8 server proofs and every server path exist; of 12 files that spawn tasks, 6 are placed, 4 are listed as not background with exact counts, and 2 were known unplaced and warned; the 40 tables the migrations leave match the 40 server stores.

A known unplaced file (metrics/periodic.rs) warns for every spawn in it until a family's paths cover it, and the not-background files fail only when their spawn count changes; any other unplaced file fails. Only file_host's src is scanned, lexically.

objectives.claim: Every check the server runs on a pull request can stop its merge.
objectives.requirement: main in the server requires one gate that waits on every pull request check, path-filtered ones such as Check some-ui against it included, and reads a skipped check as passed only where its paths did not change.
objectives.conclusion: main in the server now requires PR gate, which waits on every pull request check and fails if any fails, is cancelled or never appears, so a red Check some-ui against it, infra_ci or Assurance ledger now stops a merge; a job allowed to fail (deny's advisories, the client steps under client-breaking-route), a job skipped for any reason, and a pull request that edits gate.yml still get through (gate-verdict.yml runs main's copy, so editing it does not).

families.name: Home tells me when something goes wrong
families.why: An error on home that nobody hears of is a failure that is silent, however loudly it was logged; and a home that errors every time it is used is not working, even when each request answers.

objectives.requirement: Every ERROR-level event on home is counted by its target and its name; an alert reaches the owner within 15 minutes and says what failed, its delivery tested; and a sanitised record, one open issue per fingerprint updated in place and holding no field value, survives for the next session.
objectives.conclusion: An error alert per module reaches you (shown on 2026-10-30), but it cannot say what failed, and nothing keeps a record past the session that saw it.

evidence.says: ErrorEventMetricsLayer counts every ERROR event the log filter passes into tracing_events_total, by target alone.
The one error alert sends Slack a message per target.
On home on 2026-10-30, the error alert for opentelemetry_sdk reached the owner's Slack.

objectives.claim: Home runs nearly error-free: at least 99% of the hours in any 7 days have no error.

On home on 2026-10-30, the error alert fired for opentelemetry_sdk with 180 errors in 15 minutes: server#545 happens on home too, not only in the reproduction.

families.name: Home's one machine is shared, and what it costs is heard
families.why: Home is one machine with no swap. Several services share it, and each has its own clock, cap and retries. Renders are the lowest class, run only when there is room and give way when anything else needs it (the owner, 2026-11-07: no clock, no window), and every kill the kernel makes for memory reaches the owner.

objectives.claim: Every process the kernel kills on home for memory is heard, and named when it can be.
objectives.requirement: Every OOM kill the kernel counts on home (node_vmstat_oom_kill, inside a container's cap or across the host) fires an alert within the hour that reaches the owner: HomeOomKill naming the container cAdvisor attributes it to, or HomeOomKillUnattributed when the kernel counted more kills than cAdvisor named, held 2 minutes so one counter scraped before the other is not a kill. A second kill within the hour is the same firing alert; WHO DUNNIT's OOM tile counts each kill. Tolerance: a kill made while Prometheus was down for more than an hour shows on the tile, and no alert says it.
objectives.conclusion: Both alerts read the kernel's own count, and promtool cases prove each fires on a kill and stays quiet without one, including a kill cAdvisor did not name.

evidence.says: promtool cases for HomeOomKill and HomeOomKillUnattributed, each firing and quiet.
What each kill costs each service, and who is killed first (oom_score_adj by class).

objectives.claim: The lane that decides when renders run is heard when it stops deciding, when a job is stuck, and when it cannot read a signal.
objectives.requirement: file_host's lane writes its decision every 5 s. LaneStale fires when none was written for over a minute (one never written included); LaneStuck when the job in progress was stopped for memory or pressure stuck_after times in a row (LA4); LaneSignalsUnreadable when a signal it reads has been unreadable for 5 minutes, naming it, so a kernel without PSI is heard. file_host not answering a scrape is FileHostDown's.
objectives.conclusion: Each alert has a promtool case that fires and one that stays quiet; the CALL dashboard's LANE row shows what the lane decided and why.

evidence.says: promtool cases for LaneStale, LaneStuck and LaneSignalsUnreadable, each firing and quiet.
The lane's tick, its decision file and its metrics.

objectives.claim: A render never runs while home's interactive work waits: it pauses, or does not start.
objectives.requirement: While a voice note is heard or a Rust Rounds program recorded, the lane says pause (or does not say run), and the render worker freezes the recorder and everything it started (SIGSTOP), keeping its memory and taking no CPU, and thaws it once the lane says run again.
objectives.conclusion: The decision is a pure function held by its tests, and the render worker's obedience by its shell test with a fake lane and recorder. Home has not yet been watched pausing a real render.

evidence.says: crates/lane's step decides pause whenever interactive work waits.
A pause freezes the recorder and what it started, and the render then finishes with the same bytes, its steps made once.

objectives.claim: A render starts only with room for its peak above the floor, held for the hold-down; a reading that failed, or no peak, is never room.
objectives.requirement: Batch work starts, or starts again after a stop, only when MemAvailable leaves room for its peak above the floor and memory pressure is under its limit, both held for the hold-down. The peak is the measured one or, before any is measured, the declared ceiling. While the lane says run, a job not seen before keeps that permission only while that room holds. An unreadable signal or a missing peak is never room.
objectives.conclusion: Held by the lane's tests; the worker starts only on a run decision written after its job id was, also tested.

evidence.says: The policy home runs: 2 GiB floor, 10% some avg10, 30 s hold-down.
No render starts on a missing or stale decision, nor before the lane has seen the job.

objectives.claim: A render running or paused lets go of its memory once home runs short, and resumes from its kept steps.
objectives.requirement: Once free memory falls under the floor, memory pressure passes its limit, or a signal can no longer be read, the lane says stop and the worker kills the recorder's tree, keeps the work and the job's id, and resumes later from the step cache, paying only for the step in flight. A stop is never a failure.
objectives.conclusion: Held by the lane's tests, and the worker's stop and resume by its shell test, with the same bytes as a render never stopped.

evidence.says: A stop kills the recorder and what it started, keeps the work and the job's id, and the render resumes from its kept steps with the same bytes.

objectives.claim: A render that never fits is reported as stuck, not retried silently.
objectives.requirement: Stops for memory or pressure are counted against the job in progress, named by an id the worker keeps through pauses and stops; from stuck_after (3 on home) in a row the lane says the job is stuck and LaneStuck fires. Another id, or none, starts the count again, so an idle lane is never stuck.
objectives.conclusion: Held by the lane's tests; LaneStuck's promtool cases are LN3's.

evidence.says: LaneStuck fires on a stuck job and stays quiet otherwise.
